Abstract
The rapid growth of digital research resources has made it increasingly difficult for users
to retrieve precise and trustworthy information from large collections of documents. Tra-
ditional search systems often return keyword-based results without understanding the
semantic meaning of user queries. Moreover, Large Language Models (LLMs), although
powerful, may generate responses that are not supported by reliable sources.
This project presents the design and development of an Intelligent Research Assistant
based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The system combines modern Natural
Language Processing techniques with semantic document retrieval to provide accurate,
context-aware, and source-grounded answers.
The application has been developed using FastAPI as the backend framework with
JWT-based authentication, SQLAlchemy for relational database management, MongoDB
for document storage, Sentence Transformers for embedding generation, FAISS for effi-
cient vector similarity search, and Ollama running the Llama 3 model as the local Large
Language Model.
The complete workflow includes secure user authentication, workspace management,
document upload and preprocessing, text chunking, embedding generation, vector in-
dexing, semantic retrieval, prompt construction, LLM-based response generation, and
automatic citation generation. By restricting responses to the retrieved document con-
text, the system significantly reduces hallucinations while improving answer reliability
and transparency.
The developed system demonstrates the practical implementation of Retrieval-Augmented
Generation for research assistance and provides a scalable architecture for future integra-
tion with multiple LLMs, cloud deployment, multilingual support, and advanced docu-
ment analytics.
